title: 2nd Stopping Place 1st Truth Grandeur And Sublimity

questions.question: What is the first truth named in the passage?
questions.answer: It is the truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: Why does the passage keep the discussion of the first truth brief?
questions.answer: Because fuller proofs are said to be explained elsewhere.

questions.question: What wide-reaching pattern in creation is used to point to one Creator?
questions.answer: The same Being creates and governs things spread across vast distances at the same time and in a unified way.

questions.question: How does the passage use flowers to support its point about Divine unity?
questions.answer: It says countless flowers of the same kind appear across the earth together and with the same pattern, which points to one Maker.

questions.question: What seasonal event is described as a large-scale sign of reviving life?
questions.answer: Spring is described as bringing huge numbers of living beings back in an orderly way.

questions.question: About how many kinds of plants and animals are mentioned as being managed in a short period?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand kinds.

questions.question: What qualities mark the care of those living kinds in spring?
questions.answer: Regularity, balance, and freedom from confusion, flaw, and mistake.

questions.question: What earlier event does the springtime renewal help people recognize as possible?
questions.answer: It helps show the possibility of the creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: Besides creating living beings, what cosmic motion is mentioned?
questions.answer: The turning of the earth and the alternation of night and day.

questions.question: What human inner reality is also said to be known and governed by the same Being?
questions.answer: Even the most hidden thoughts in people’s hearts.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from these many actions being treated as one act?
questions.answer: Their Doer must be one unique and powerful Being.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does this grandeur leave no room for?
questions.answer: It leaves no room at all for any partner.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the effect of this grandeur on the idea of shirk?
questions.answer: It says such grandeur does not merely weaken that idea but removes it completely.

questions.question: Why would allowing a partner imply a problem in relation to Divine power?
questions.answer: It would suggest weakness or need in that power.

questions.question: Why would allowing a partner be an insult to Divine greatness?
questions.answer: It would treat Divine glory, loftiness, and perfection as if they were lacking.

questions.question: What would attributing partners imply about Divine perfection and comprehensiveness?
questions.answer: It would imply defect in perfection and limits on what is all-encompassing.

questions.question: How does the passage evaluate this idea from the standpoint of reason?
questions.answer: It says no sound mind would accept it as possible.

questions.question: Why is assigning partners presented as an especially serious sin?
questions.answer: Because it violates Allah’s grandeur, glory, and sublimity.

questions.question: What Qur’anic ruling is mentioned to show the seriousness of shirk?
questions.answer: The passage says that associating partners with Allah is not forgiven, while lesser sins may be forgiven.

questions.question: What is the second truth introduced after the first?
questions.answer: It is the absoluteness, comprehensiveness, and boundless appearance of dominical deeds in the cosmos.

questions.question: What limits those deeds, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Only Allah’s wisdom and will, along with the capacities of the things and places where those deeds appear.

questions.question: Which five alternatives are rejected as real causes of these orderly deeds?
questions.answer: Chance, nature, force, causality, and the elements.

questions.question: Why are those alternatives rejected?
questions.answer: Because they cannot produce deeds that are so balanced, wise, life-giving, orderly, and firm.

questions.question: If those things are not true causes, what role do they play?
questions.answer: They serve only as an outward veil through Allah’s command, will, and power.

questions.question: How many examples does the passage say will be given for this second truth?
questions.answer: Three examples.

questions.question: From where are those three examples said to come?
questions.answer: They come from three connected verses in Surat al-Nahl.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the reach of the Creator’s activity among the stars?
questions.answer: It says stars separated by enormous distances are created and governed together.

questions.question: How does the passage use the spread of flowers across the earth?
questions.answer: It presents their simultaneous and similar creation across different regions as evidence of one command.

questions.question: What time frame is given for the ordering of many plant and animal kinds?
questions.answer: Five or six weeks.

questions.question: What does the spring season display before human eyes, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Many examples of revival after deathlike stillness.

questions.question: Which daily cycle is mentioned as another sign of Divine control?
questions.answer: The joining of night and day into one another.

questions.question: What image is used for the night in relation to the day?
questions.answer: Night is pictured like a page carrying the record of daytime events.

questions.question: What does the same Being also know about human beings?
questions.answer: The most hidden thoughts inside their hearts.

questions.question: Why does the passage gather all these activities into a single act?
questions.answer: To show that one and the same Doer carries them out.

questions.question: What does that single-act argument say about the identity of the Doer?
questions.answer: The Doer must be uniquely one and fully powerful.

questions.question: In what three ways does the passage say partnership would wrong Divine reality?
questions.answer: It would imply weakness, fault, and limitation.

questions.question: What would be wrongly ascribed to Divine power if a partner were accepted?
questions.answer: Need or inability.

questions.question: What would be wrongly ascribed to Divine grandeur if a partner were accepted?
questions.answer: A stain of deficiency.

questions.question: What would be wrongly ascribed to Divine perfection if a partner were accepted?
questions.answer: Imperfection.

questions.question: What would be wrongly ascribed to Divine all-encompassing reach if a partner were accepted?
questions.answer: Restriction.

questions.question: What judgment does the passage make about the sound intellect and shirk?
questions.answer: A sound intellect would not count it as possible.

questions.question: How is the sin of assigning partners morally characterized?
questions.answer: It is presented as an extremely grave offense against Allah’s majesty.

questions.question: What is the second truth mainly about?
questions.answer: It is about the unlimited and universal character of Allah’s governing acts in the universe.

questions.question: What alone determines the measure and form of those acts?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, together with the capacities of created things.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the rejected alternatives like chance and nature?
questions.answer: It describes them as lacking awareness, order, and true control.

questions.question: What kind of deeds are said to be beyond the power of those alternatives?
questions.answer: Deeds that are measured, wise, insightful, life-giving, orderly, and firm.

questions.question: What function is left to these apparent causes?
questions.answer: They are only outward means or coverings, not independent makers.

questions.question: Through what are those outward means employed?
questions.answer: Through the command, will, and power of the Glorious Doer.

questions.question: Why does the passage announce three examples at the end?
questions.answer: To prepare the reader for concrete illustrations of the second truth.

questions.question: What does the phrase about countless examples imply even before the examples begin?
questions.answer: It implies that the signs are far more numerous than the three selected ones.

questions.question: What is the core claim of the first truth in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s unmatched greatness and loftiness rule out any partner.

questions.question: How does the passage connect distant stars and earthly life?
questions.answer: It says the same Being manages both, showing one universal control.

questions.question: Why is the simultaneous creation of similar flowers across the world important in the argument?
questions.answer: It shows unified action that fits one Creator rather than many separate powers.

questions.question: What does the treatment of hundreds of thousands of life-forms in a few weeks show?
questions.answer: It shows vast power joined with precision and order.

questions.question: What qualities prevent that springtime activity from being seen as random?
questions.answer: Its consistency, balance, and freedom from error.

questions.question: How is spring presented in relation to resurrection?
questions.answer: It is shown as a repeated sign that bringing life back is fully possible.

questions.question: What natural process involving the earth supports the theme of Divine rule?
questions.answer: The ongoing alternation of night and day through the earth’s movement.

questions.question: What is striking about Allah’s knowledge in addition to His outward control?
questions.answer: His knowledge reaches even hidden inner thoughts.

questions.question: What logical step does the passage make after listing many acts?
questions.answer: It says they are truly one act and so come from one Doer.

questions.question: What kind of Being must that Doer be?
questions.answer: A single, powerful, glorious Being.

questions.question: Does the passage present room for partial partnership in Divine action?
questions.answer: No, it says there is no opening at all for that.

questions.question: What does the passage say grandeur itself does to the possibility of partnership?
questions.answer: It removes that possibility completely.

questions.question: Why would partnership conflict with absolute power?
questions.answer: Because it would imply power that is not fully sufficient by itself.

questions.question: Why would partnership conflict with perfection?
questions.answer: Because true perfection does not admit defect.

questions.question: Why would partnership conflict with all-encompassing rule?
questions.answer: Because sharing would mean that rule is limited.

questions.question: What kind of intellect rejects the idea of shirk according to the passage?
questions.answer: A healthy and sound intellect.

questions.question: Why is shirk not treated as just another error?
questions.answer: Because it directly violates Allah’s majesty, glory, and loftiness.

questions.question: What Qur’anic principle is cited to underline the seriousness of this sin?
questions.answer: That associating partners with Allah is not forgiven, unlike lesser sins.

questions.question: What three features define the second truth?
questions.answer: Its absoluteness, its comprehensiveness, and its appearing without limit.

questions.question: Where are these dominical deeds seen at work?
questions.answer: Throughout the cosmos.

questions.question: What two things set the bounds for how these deeds appear?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, and the capacities of created recipients.

questions.question: What is said about chance, nature, force, causality, and the elements?
questions.answer: They cannot share in these acts as real causes.

questions.question: What traits of the deeds make those alternatives impossible?
questions.answer: Their wisdom, balance, life-giving quality, order, and firmness.

questions.question: How does the passage reinterpret visible causes?
questions.answer: As coverings that hide direct power, not as independent agents.

questions.question: What lies behind those coverings in reality?
questions.answer: The command, will, and power of Allah.

questions.question: What teaching method does the passage use after stating the second truth?
questions.answer: It moves from a general claim to three specific examples.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the first truth called?
questions.answer: The truth of grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: Why does the passage not fully expand every proof for that truth here?
questions.answer: Because detailed proofs are said to exist in other places.

questions.question: What does creating stars far apart in one manner show?
questions.answer: It shows control that is single, unified, and not divided among partners.

questions.question: What does producing the same type of flower across the globe at one time suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests one will and one act behind them.

questions.question: What number of plant and animal kinds is mentioned in the discussion of spring?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand.

questions.question: What is remarkable about how those many kinds are handled?
questions.answer: They are managed quickly and perfectly without disorder or mistake.

questions.question: What does the passage say spring places before human sight?
questions.answer: Many examples of renewed life on earth.

questions.question: What movement involving time is mentioned along with the earth’s motion?
questions.answer: The entrance of night into day and day into night.

questions.question: How far does Divine knowledge reach in human beings, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It reaches the most hidden thoughts of the heart.

questions.question: Why are these many different operations counted as one act?
questions.answer: Because they all come from the same direct command and administration.

questions.question: What follows from that unity of action?
questions.answer: The actor is one unique and powerful Being.

questions.question: What does the passage say about any chance for another being to share in this rule?
questions.answer: It says there is not even the slightest chance.

questions.question: What four wrong ideas would accepting a partner force onto Divine attributes?
questions.answer: Weakness, need, defect, and limitation.

questions.question: Which Divine attribute would seem needy if partnership were allowed?
questions.answer: Divine power.

questions.question: Which Divine attribute would seem flawed if partnership were allowed?
questions.answer: Divine grandeur.

questions.question: Which Divine attribute would seem incomplete if partnership were allowed?
questions.answer: Divine perfection.

questions.question: Which Divine attribute would seem restricted if partnership were allowed?
questions.answer: Divine all-encompassing scope.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the seriousness of shirk in relation to Allah’s honor?
questions.answer: It is a major offense against His majesty and glory.

questions.question: What is the main subject of the second truth?
questions.answer: The universal and unrestricted character of Allah’s dominical acts.

questions.question: What limits those acts from spreading in every possible way?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, plus the capacities of creatures and places.

questions.question: Why can blind force and unconscious causality not be true agents here?
questions.answer: Because the deeds display intelligence, order, life, and stable purpose.

questions.question: What is said about the elements that are scattered everywhere?
questions.answer: They also cannot be partners in these wise and measured acts.

questions.question: What role is assigned to visible causes instead?
questions.answer: They function only as outward screens.

questions.question: What actually uses those screens?
questions.answer: Allah’s command, will, and power.

questions.question: What does the passage promise next after introducing the second truth?
questions.answer: It promises three examples drawn from connected verses in Surat al-Nahl.

questions.question: What theme stands at the center of the first truth?
questions.answer: Allah’s supreme majesty and loftiness.

questions.question: How does the passage use the order of the universe to support tawhid?
questions.answer: It points to one Being who creates and governs many levels of existence in one coordinated way.

questions.question: Why are stars mentioned as being very far from one another?
questions.answer: To stress the vast range of one and the same Divine action.

questions.question: Why are flowers in different directions of the earth mentioned together?
questions.answer: To show simultaneous creation of similar beings across the world.

questions.question: What does the passage highlight about spring besides beauty?
questions.answer: It highlights mass renewal of life with exact order.

questions.question: What makes that renewal a proof rather than just a seasonal habit?
questions.answer: It happens with precision, balance, and no confusion across huge numbers of species.

questions.question: What past act does this seasonal renewal help confirm?
questions.answer: The creation of the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What daily sign of rule is added after the discussion of spring?
questions.answer: The changing of night into day and day into night.

questions.question: What human dimension is included alongside cosmic events?
questions.answer: Inner thoughts and secrets of the heart.

questions.question: What does the passage conclude from one Being handling both cosmic and inner realities?
questions.answer: His power and knowledge are uniquely universal.

questions.question: How does the passage define the collected activities it lists?
questions.answer: It treats them as one act in reality.

questions.question: What does that say about the Doer?
questions.answer: The Doer is one unique and powerful Lord.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Divine grandeur and partnership in this argument?
questions.answer: Divine grandeur completely blocks the idea of partnership.

questions.question: Why would shirk amount to attributing weakness?
questions.answer: Because sharing rule would imply the need for support.

questions.question: Why would shirk amount to attributing fault?
questions.answer: Because it would make Divine greatness seem less than perfect.

questions.question: Why would shirk amount to attributing limits?
questions.answer: Because shared authority would deny all-encompassing control.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is used when the passage says no sound intellect accepts this?
questions.answer: It uses rational judgment based on the implications of Divine attributes.

questions.question: Why does the Qur’anic warning about shirk fit the argument here?
questions.answer: Because the passage has shown shirk to be a direct attack on Allah’s majesty.

questions.question: What is the focus of the second truth?
questions.answer: The all-reaching and unrestricted nature of Divine governing actions in the universe.

questions.question: What keeps those actions within proper measure?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, and the capacities of what receives those actions.

questions.question: What false explanations are dismissed?
questions.answer: Randomness, nature, force, causality, and material elements.

questions.question: What kind of acts are they unable to produce?
questions.answer: Acts that are balanced, wise, life-giving, orderly, and firmly established.

questions.question: If they are not real makers, how are they presented?
questions.answer: As outward means used under Divine command.

questions.question: Why is the idea of a veil important in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that visible causes hide direct Divine power without replacing it.

questions.question: How does the passage transition toward evidence for the second truth?
questions.answer: It says three examples will be chosen from many subtle signs.

questions.question: What is the name of the first truth discussed in the marked passage?
questions.answer: Grandeur and sublimity.

questions.question: What does the passage say about where fuller arguments for this truth can be found?
questions.answer: It says they are explained elsewhere, so only a brief treatment is given here.

questions.question: How does the passage portray the creation and administration of stars?
questions.answer: As occurring together under one pattern despite immense distances.

questions.question: What does the simultaneous appearance of countless flowers of one species indicate?
questions.answer: It indicates one Maker acting with one command.

questions.question: How many broad kinds of plants and animals are said to be managed in spring?
questions.answer: More than two hundred thousand.

questions.question: What short period is given for that management?
questions.answer: Five or six weeks.

questions.question: Which qualities of that management are emphasized?
questions.answer: Exactness, balance, and complete freedom from confusion and error.

questions.question: Why is spring compared to a great revival?
questions.answer: Because it brings countless living examples back into existence.

questions.question: What unseen or past reality does this visible revival help verify?
questions.answer: The mighty act of creating the heavens and the earth.

questions.question: What ongoing sign involving time and motion is mentioned next?
questions.answer: The passing of night into day and day into night through the earth’s turning.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s knowledge of people?
questions.answer: He knows and directs even the most hidden thoughts in their hearts.

questions.question: Why does the passage say all the acts mentioned are really one act?
questions.answer: Because they come from one source of command and governance.

questions.question: What must be true of the One who performs that act?
questions.answer: He is uniquely one and possesses great power.

questions.question: What possibility is completely denied because of that majesty?
questions.answer: Any possibility of a partner sharing in Divine action.

questions.question: In the passage’s reasoning, what would partnership wrongly suggest about Divine power?
questions.answer: That it has weakness or need.

questions.question: What would partnership wrongly suggest about Divine greatness and perfection?
questions.answer: That they contain fault or deficiency.

questions.question: What would partnership wrongly suggest about Divine comprehensiveness?
questions.answer: That it is limited.

questions.question: How does the passage appeal to human reason on this issue?
questions.answer: It says a sound intellect cannot accept such implications.

questions.question: Why is shirk described as an enormous crime?
questions.answer: Because it offends Allah’s grandeur, glory, and sublime rank.

questions.question: What is the second truth called in substance?
questions.answer: The absolute, comprehensive, and limitless appearance of Divine lordly acts.

questions.question: In what arena are these acts observed?
questions.answer: In the whole cosmos.

questions.question: What gives these acts their limits and fitting forms?
questions.answer: Allah’s wisdom and will, along with the capacities of created things and places.

questions.question: Which supposed causes are said to have no real share in these acts?
questions.answer: Chance, nature, force, causality, and the elements.

questions.question: What features of the acts make those supposed causes impossible?
questions.answer: Their balance, wisdom, clarity of purpose, life-giving effect, order, and firmness.

questions.question: What role do those supposed causes actually play?
questions.answer: They are only outward coverings or instruments.

questions.question: Under whose control are those coverings used?
questions.answer: Under the command, will, and power of the Glorious Doer.

questions.question: What does the passage say it will do next to explain this second truth?
questions.answer: It will present three examples from consecutive verses in Surat al-Nahl.
